channel.title: Nature Materials
channel.description: Nature Materials is a multidisciplinary journal aimed at bringing together cutting-edge research across the entire spectrum of materials science and technology. Nature Materials covers all applied and fundamental aspects of the synthesis/processing, structure/composition, properties and performance of materials. Nature Materials provides a forum for the development of a common identity among materials scientists while encouraging researchers to cross established subdisciplinary lines. To achieve this, Nature Materials takes an interdisciplinary, integrated and balanced approach to all areas of materials research while fostering the exchange of ideas between scientists involved in different communities.

item.title: [7] Spin currents in polariton waveguides driven by bright and dark excitons
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Weibo Gao, Jesús Zúñiga-Pérez

Authors: Qiuyu Shang, Mingyang Zhang, Maria V. Maggi, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of spin currents and optical spin Hall effect in 2D WS2, relevant to van der Waals systems.

Tags: #2Dmaterials #vanderWaals #spintronics #optical #Halleffect

Abstract: Non-resonant excitation of WS2 in-plane microcavities generates waveguide exciton–polaritons that carry spin-polarized currents over distances exceeding 90 μm at room temperature and reveal a non-resonantly pumped optical spin Hall effect.

item.title: [6] Writing monolayer oxides with electrons
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Ali Zavabeti

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Methodology for creating novel free-standing monolayer oxide materials using electron beam.

Tags: #materialssynthesis #2Dmaterials #microscopy #methodology

Abstract: Layered metal oxyhalides can be selectively dehalogenated inside a scanning transmission electron microscope, yielding free-standing monolayer oxide sheets and coupling synthesis with atomic-resolution observation.

item.title: [6] Topological control of polaritonic flatbands in anisotropic van der Waals metasurfaces
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Alexander A. Antonov, Andreas Tittl

Authors: Connor Heimig, Thomas Weber, Cristina Cruciano, et al.

Score 6/10 C_MAYBE

Why: Topological control of polaritonic flatbands in an anisotropic van der Waals material.

Tags: #vanderWaals #topological #photonics #light-matterinteraction

Abstract: Photonic metasurfaces patterned in anisotropic ReS2 create robust, spectrally scalable directional photonic flatbands, enabling the topological control of polarization-resolved exciton–polaritons and enhanced light–matter coupling.

item.title: [7] Free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides at the single-atomic-layer limit
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Hong-Jun Gao, Wu Zhou

Authors: Meng Gao, Deping Guo, Ang Li, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Method for fabricating free-standing 2D materials, heterostructures, and twisted bilayers.

Tags: #materialssynthesis #2Dmaterials #heterostructure #twistedbilayer #methodology

Abstract: The electron-beam-assisted subtraction method enables the controllable fabrication of free-standing metal oxide monolayers, along with lateral heterostructures and twisted bilayers, expanding the material space of 2D quantum systems.
